title: Grateful Dead Live at Madison Square Garden on 1982-09-21
lineage: Sennheiser 421's (18th row - Center) > Sony TC-D5 > Master Cassette > Playback on Nak Dragon > Sony R700 DAT deck (sbm-on) - used only as A>D converter (44.1khz) > ZA2 > CDR (x1)  > EAC(tracked with Addawav & CDWav) >SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy fall ’82 show highlighted by a smoking Playin’ > Crazy Fingers opener and standout early Touch of Grey.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean soundboard mix that lets the band’s tight, high‑octane performance shine. Reviewers rave about the blistering opening sequence (Playin’ into Crazy Fingers), the embryonic but magical Touch of Grey, and strong renditions of High Time, Good Lovin’, and West L.A., while noting only minor drum mud‑iness. Overall the show is described as one of the best New York/East Coast dates of 1982.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both performance and soundboard quality across >10 reviews; minor technical quibbles keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mix praised by multiple reviewers; a few note slightly trashy drum tones and occasional modest sound issues but overall excellent for a soundboard source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The show opens with a blazing Playin’ > Crazy Fingers sequence that sets a high‑energy tone, then flows through early Touch of Grey and solid mid‑set numbers like High Time before closing with fan‑favorite Good Lovin’ and West L.A.; the pacing is described as seamless and exciting.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as 'ripping leads' and delivering a spectacular solo throughout the opener.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for thunderous bass that even rattles sub‑woofers.
band_member_comments.Bob: His vocal rap on Good Lovin’ is called a classic; noted for strong rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (keyboardist) highlighted for funky organ riffs throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Generally solid but a few reviewers mention the drum sound being a bit trashy or muddy.
